title: Moriz homepage — section-by-section design research
scope: Independent UX/UI design and development studio; existing confirmed homepage sections.
method: Five references per section, combining inspected Mobbin section captures with verified Siteinspire listings and checked live-site content. References recur when relevant to different sections. Observations describe sources; adaptations and recommendations are design judgments, not measured conversion findings.
limits: Mobbin capture dates are unavailable. Siteinspire publication dates identify listing dates, not website launch dates. Most Siteinspire references were checked through live content rather than a full rendered visual audit; MONOLOG’s project row was also visually inspected. Mobile, Hebrew/RTL, motion and accessibility behavior need separate exploration.
constraints: Retain the confirmed homepage order, approved Mammoth-based hero trial and one hero project-viewing action. The logo carousel is a supplementary block. Keep WhatsApp floating-only. Starting steps remain a 5–10 minute call, an in-depth specification discussion, and a quote. FAQ answers and contact content are still open.

sections.title: Hero
sections.purpose: Make the studio’s offer understandable and lead into the work.
sections.recommendation: Use Nick Clement for positioning clarity and Unseen for headline hierarchy. Compare these against the already selected Mammoth Murals composition; the research does not replace that trial.

examples.name: Unseen Studio
examples.observation: Centered headline, short agency descriptor and visible work button over an immersive scene.
examples.adaptation: Separate the expressive headline, concrete UX/UI and development explanation, and one project-viewing action.
examples.limitation: The scene is visually dominant. Atmosphere alone does not communicate what Moriz delivers.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Locomotive
examples.observation: Large studio name and a compact digital-agency descriptor sit over a full-bleed red portrait.
examples.adaptation: Study how a strong name and short descriptor can establish personality without numerous competing elements.
examples.limitation: The captured region offers little service explanation. This is a boldness reference rather than a complete Moriz hero.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Nick Clement
examples.observation: A concise value proposition is followed by a personal product-design introduction and supporting service explanation.
examples.adaptation: Make the offer understandable before asking visitors to interpret the visual style.
examples.limitation: The quiet personal positioning is a different expressive direction from the approved Mammoth trial.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

examples.name: MONOLOG
examples.observation: The opening connects website and identity work to client ambition, then offers an introductory conversation.
examples.adaptation: Connect the creative headline to a concrete client need in the supporting sentence.
examples.limitation: Its booking action differs from Moriz’s selected hero action. Borrow the positioning logic.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

examples.name: Special Offer Inc
examples.observation: The studio frames its offer around creative technology and brings together design and technical disciplines.
examples.adaptation: Make design and development read as parts of one studio offer.
examples.limitation: A broad creative-technology umbrella can obscure the more specific UX/UI and website services.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

sections.title: Client logo strip — supplementary
sections.purpose: Add compact evidence of relevant experience immediately after the introduction.
sections.recommendation: Compare Fiasco’s distributed logos with Givingli’s restrained strip. Keep the already authorized carousel; use the references to study scale and density.

examples.name: Fiasco
examples.observation: Two widely spaced rows of logos sit with a short introductory caption.
examples.adaptation: Use consistent optical sizing so recognizable names support the message without overpowering it.
examples.limitation: The larger two-row block uses more vertical space than a compact strip; motion is not established by this still.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: basement.studio
examples.observation: A studio introduction leads into a dense bordered matrix of client logos.
examples.adaptation: Study consistent cell alignment and the separation between positioning and proof.
examples.limitation: A full wall is disproportionate to a small client set; it is a grid alternative, not the selected carousel.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Givingli
examples.observation: A small trust caption accompanies a narrow horizontal logo band.
examples.adaptation: Keep a short caption and a restrained vertical footprint.
examples.limitation: This is a product-company reference. Reuse its proportions, not its customer positioning.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: MONOLOG
examples.observation: A recognizable-client name strip supports the studio introduction.
examples.adaptation: Keep the proof close to the positioning and distinguish studio clients from other professional experience.
examples.limitation: Text names do not demonstrate a logo treatment; brand recognition varies by audience.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

examples.name: Otherkind
examples.observation: Past engagements are listed with dates.
examples.adaptation: Consider factual engagement labels when a logo needs context about the owner’s role.
examples.limitation: This is a text-based proof alternative, not a logo carousel example.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

sections.title: Three communication themes
sections.purpose: Explain research-based specification, an engaging interactive experience, and development.
sections.recommendation: Metalab offers the clearest benefit-led reference; Raw Materials supplies a useful comparison for organizing three disciplines. Keep Moriz’s three selected themes rather than expanding into a full service catalogue.

examples.name: Metalab
examples.observation: Large benefit headlines lead rows with supporting explanation; discipline lists follow below.
examples.adaptation: Make each theme a client benefit with one concrete sentence explaining how the studio delivers it.
examples.limitation: Its full capabilities block is longer than this homepage section needs.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Raw Materials
examples.observation: Design, Strategy and Technology form three parallel columns of services.
examples.adaptation: Use equal visual weight for three distinct but connected strengths.
examples.limitation: Long service lists can make the section feel like a catalogue; Moriz’s themes need much less detail.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Aino Agency
examples.observation: Restrained capability lists use a clear column structure with small supporting links.
examples.adaptation: Explore a quiet, scannable treatment that leaves attention available for the projects.
examples.limitation: Lists communicate scope more readily than value; add concise benefit explanations.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Little Plains
examples.observation: Design, Technology and Hospitality are articulated as separate principles with explanations.
examples.adaptation: Give each Moriz theme its own meaningful heading and a short reason it matters to the client.
examples.limitation: The reference principles are specific to Little Plains; they do not become Moriz’s claims.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

examples.name: Nick Clement
examples.observation: The service explanation is grouped into Design, Strategy and Build.
examples.adaptation: Connect the research, experience and implementation messages through a simple three-part story.
examples.limitation: The grouping is content evidence; an exact three-column visual layout was not verified.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

sections.title: Projects
sections.purpose: Show the quality of the work and clarify the studio’s contribution.
sections.recommendation: Start the layout comparison with Fiasco’s staggered grid and MONOLOG’s image-plus-context rows. Keep Huncwot as the owner’s existing project-layout preference.

examples.name: Fiasco
examples.observation: Staggered project images in two columns carry names, short context and tags.
examples.adaptation: Give each selected project a visual, a one-line brief and clear contribution labels.
examples.limitation: Uneven image positions need a deliberate Hebrew reading order and a simpler mobile sequence.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Instrument
examples.observation: Different image sizes create an editorial work selection, with filtering and display controls.
examples.adaptation: Use variation to establish a featured project and a clear visual rhythm.
examples.limitation: Filters and view controls add overhead for a small portfolio; they need an actual browsing problem to solve.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Unseen Studio
examples.observation: Two large project previews sit side by side with names, short descriptions, categories and arrows.
examples.adaptation: Keep the relationship between project preview and project context explicit.
examples.limitation: The surrounding scene can compete with the work. A still does not establish hover or motion behavior.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Nick Clement
examples.observation: Selected projects pair names with short context subtitles and discipline labels.
examples.adaptation: Make the owner’s role legible, especially when presenting employed and independent experience together.
examples.limitation: Content grouping was checked; precise thumbnail proportions and responsive behavior were not audited.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

examples.name: MONOLOG
examples.observation: A large project visual is paired with contextual text and an outcome metric in a success-story row.
examples.adaptation: Connect the attractive screenshot to what the project achieved and what Moriz contributed.
examples.limitation: Only use results that Moriz can substantiate. The reference’s metrics are not transferable.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

sections.title: Brief owner introduction
sections.purpose: Help visitors understand who will work with them.
sections.recommendation: MONOLOG and Nick Clement are the closest content references for a personal studio. Kalstore gives a clear visual comparison for portrait and biography.

examples.name: Mother Design
examples.observation: A prominent studio introduction sits above a wide photograph of the real team.
examples.adaptation: Use authentic photography to put a human presence beside a short professional introduction.
examples.limitation: This is a team studio and an information-page section; adapt the scale to one owner.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Kalstore
examples.observation: A founder biography occupies one colored panel beside a large portrait.
examples.adaptation: Compare a compact portrait-and-biography split with a text-first owner introduction.
examples.limitation: The source is a furniture/design business. Its product story and commercial positioning are not relevant.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Nick Clement
examples.observation: The introduction is written personally and explains collaboration with founders and engineering teams.
examples.adaptation: Explain the owner’s expertise and how direct collaboration works in a few specific sentences.
examples.limitation: Audience and collaboration claims need to reflect the owner’s actual practice.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

examples.name: Otherkind
examples.observation: Two founders are named and the team is connected to the studio’s working model.
examples.adaptation: Make the person responsible for the work visible, with a clear role.
examples.limitation: A two-founder studio is a scale mismatch; do not imply a larger Moriz team.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

examples.name: MONOLOG
examples.observation: The founder’s headshot and name sit alongside a personal explanation of the studio.
examples.adaptation: Study how a recognizable owner identity can connect the portfolio to the person leading the engagement.
examples.limitation: Use a real owner image and voice; detailed spacing and mobile composition remain to be explored.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

sections.title: Client testimonials
sections.purpose: Provide credible third-party evidence about working with the studio.
sections.recommendation: Büro is the strongest restrained layout reference. Use MONOLOG and designmill to compare attribution and the range of client perspectives.

examples.name: Büro
examples.observation: A large quote occupies the main column while author, organization and role sit in a smaller column.
examples.adaptation: Treat the testimony and its attribution as equally necessary parts of the proof.
examples.limitation: A long quote dominates the page. This capture’s quote differs from the current live-site content.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: OFF+BRAND
examples.observation: A large introductory statement leads horizontal testimonial cards with portraits and detailed attribution.
examples.adaptation: Compare multiple compact testimonials with one featured quote.
examples.limitation: The heading and card density compete for space; a still cannot verify carousel interaction.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Analogue Agency
examples.observation: Two light quote cards contrast with a dark background and include small circular portraits.
examples.adaptation: Use a consistent card format when comparing short comments from several clients.
examples.limitation: Some text is clipped in the capture. The layout is usable evidence; the complete testimonial wording is not.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: designmill®
examples.observation: Several testimonials identify both the speaker and their company.
examples.adaptation: Use full attribution and choose comments that describe different aspects of the engagement.
examples.limitation: The live content was checked, but quote-card layout and controls were not visually audited.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

examples.name: MONOLOG
examples.observation: Client comments include author, role and company; the live page exposes previous and next controls.
examples.adaptation: Keep attribution visible and make additional quotes easy to access if a carousel is chosen.
examples.limitation: Controls establish a carousel exists, not how well it works. Approved real quotes are still required.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

sections.title: How to start working together
sections.purpose: Explain the 5–10 minute call, in-depth specification conversation and quotation.
sections.recommendation: Use Ragged Edge’s numbered hierarchy for the selected three steps, with Framer’s expectation-setting as a comparison. These references mostly describe broader collaboration or delivery; only their presentation patterns transfer.

examples.name: Ragged Edge
examples.observation: Numbered vertical stages each use a large heading and a short explanatory paragraph.
examples.adaptation: Present the three actual starting steps with a title and an explanation of what the visitor can expect.
examples.limitation: The source describes a four-stage brand journey. Do not copy its stages or imply Moriz has approved a delivery process.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Fiasco
examples.observation: A compact three-stage index sits beside the explanation and imagery of a highlighted stage.
examples.adaptation: Compare a compact step index with three fully visible explanations.
examples.limitation: The selected-state appearance does not prove tab behavior; hidden steps may be unnecessary for a short sequence.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Framer
examples.observation: A consultation introduction and kickoff action sit beside a short vertical explanation of collaboration.
examples.adaptation: State what happens when contact begins and what the first conversation is for.
examples.limitation: This is an expert-service offering on a platform. Its ongoing collaboration steps are not Moriz’s selected starting sequence.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: MONOLOG
examples.observation: Three stages explain the studio’s broader delivery journey, with examples linked alongside.
examples.adaptation: Keep step titles short and let the explanation carry practical expectations.
examples.limitation: Its delivery stages differ from call → specification discussion → quote. Reuse the communication pattern only.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

examples.name: Little Plains
examples.observation: The studio explains collaboration cadence and separates project work from a retainer arrangement.
examples.adaptation: Use concrete expectations so visitors know what the starting conversation will clarify.
examples.limitation: This is working-model content rather than an exact three-step onboarding layout; do not import unapproved cadence or retainer terms.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

sections.title: FAQ
sections.purpose: Resolve remaining questions before the contact section.
sections.recommendation: Compare Fiasco’s split layout with Büro’s numbered list. Final Moriz questions and answers remain open; the research only supplies presentation and topic-selection patterns.

examples.name: Büro
examples.observation: A dark list uses numbered questions, horizontal rules and expandable-answer affordances.
examples.adaptation: Explore strong question hierarchy and a clear distinction between collapsed and open states.
examples.limitation: The captured seven-question list differs from the current contact page. Its questions do not automatically fit Moriz.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Fiasco
examples.observation: A heading occupies one side while ruled question rows occupy the other; one answer is open.
examples.adaptation: Keep the section label stable while visitors scan concise questions.
examples.limitation: A split layout needs a mobile stack and Hebrew reading-order check; keyboard behavior is not established by the still.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Readymag
examples.observation: Questions and visible answers are grouped in two columns with contrasting dark question headers.
examples.adaptation: Compare an answer-visible format with a compact accordion.
examples.limitation: This is a web-creation product. Its support, hosting and plan questions need different treatment for a studio.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Pear
examples.observation: A short question-and-answer group addresses the unusual commercial model and likely objections.
examples.adaptation: Select questions from actual client uncertainty and answer directly.
examples.limitation: Pear’s revenue-sharing model is unrelated. This is an objection-handling reference; accordion behavior was not verified.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

examples.name: MONOLOG
examples.observation: Questions address founder involvement, timing, communication, getting started and post-launch work.
examples.adaptation: Use the client’s practical concerns as a filter for deciding what belongs in the FAQ.
examples.limitation: Topics are prompts for investigation, not approved Moriz answers, timelines or service promises.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

sections.title: Contact
sections.purpose: End with a clear invitation and an understandable next action.
sections.recommendation: Compare basement’s concentrated invitation with MONOLOG’s personal ending. Contact content still needs selection within Moriz’s confirmed floating-only WhatsApp access.

examples.name: basement.studio
examples.observation: A short invitation leads to a prominent email address on a dark background.
examples.adaptation: Make the invitation identifiable without adding several competing messages.
examples.limitation: Email is the reference’s channel. It does not authorize an inline WhatsApp action or a new Moriz contact channel.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Fiasco
examples.observation: An oversized inquiry prompt creates a dramatic final contact region.
examples.adaptation: Study scale and whitespace as ways to mark the end of the homepage.
examples.limitation: The crop does not show a complete form or contact flow; large lettering must still communicate a useful next step.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Unseen Studio
examples.observation: A contact title, inquiry-type choices and email sit over an immersive scene.
examples.adaptation: Compare direct contact with a lightly guided inquiry.
examples.limitation: Routing choices need real destinations; the scene can reduce practical clarity.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Special Offer Inc
examples.observation: The contact explanation describes suitable work and provides a direct email route.
examples.adaptation: Use one concise sentence to help a prospective client recognize when to contact the studio.
examples.limitation: Do not adopt the source’s email channel or project criteria without a content decision.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

examples.name: MONOLOG
examples.observation: A final introductory-conversation invitation is paired with a candid founder-at-work image.
examples.adaptation: Connect the invitation to the person the visitor will actually speak with.
examples.limitation: Its booking flow is separate from Moriz’s agreed access pattern; the contact section still needs its own content decision.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

sections.title: Footer
sections.purpose: Provide compact navigation, identity and necessary secondary information.
sections.recommendation: Nick Clement is the best scale reference for an independent owner. Compare Fiasco’s grouping and Structured’s minimal density before selecting Moriz’s footer content.

examples.name: Fiasco
examples.observation: Navigation and social groups sit beside a newsletter area, with policies and copyright below.
examples.adaptation: Separate useful navigation from legal and identity information.
examples.limitation: The newsletter adds another conversion goal; include one only if the studio actually needs it.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Locomotive
examples.observation: Three groups organize menu, social and external links, with expressive contact typography below.
examples.adaptation: Use clear groups and generous separation to keep the footer scannable.
examples.limitation: The expressive contact block could duplicate the preceding contact section.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Structured
examples.observation: A large wordmark is paired with a narrow link list and a small copyright/privacy line.
examples.adaptation: Compare a strong identity with a very small secondary navigation footprint.
examples.limitation: Use the footer composition only; the source’s scale and brand treatment are not a Moriz brand direction.
examples.evidence: Mobbin section image visually inspected; capture date unavailable.

examples.name: Nick Clement
examples.observation: The ending includes contact/social destinations, location or status information and legal identity.
examples.adaptation: Scale the footer to an independent practitioner rather than a large agency sitemap.
examples.limitation: Availability and location information can become stale; include it only when maintained.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.

examples.name: MONOLOG
examples.observation: The footer groups navigation, studio details and social destinations, alongside several extra utilities.
examples.adaptation: Group the essential secondary links into a short, predictable ending.
examples.limitation: Its clocks and AI-prompt utilities add complexity; they have no established purpose for Moriz.
examples.evidence: Siteinspire listing and live website content checked. Detailed rendered layout and mobile states were not audited.
